contexts: The construction still requires complex dominance analysis [2] to identify loops and CFG reconstruction to convert loops into a canonical form [8].

To enable vectorization across more complex control flows, Predicated Static single-assignment (PSSA) [8] is introduced to transform the IR into a non-CFG-based form, replacing the CFG with flat list of instructions and loops and attached control predicates [8].
On PSSA [8], some optimization algorithms are proposed to perform vectorization across complex control flow such as loop fusion.
The difficulty of constructing PSSA [8] directly from LLVM IR are mainly about structure analysis, like dominance analysis, and transformation.
And constructing appropriate control predicates [8] also requires dominance analysis [2] and even incomplete heuristics [8].
Nevertheless, constructing PSSA [8] directly from LLVM IR is nontrivial.
The level two IR, VIR, is a non-CFG-based IR derived from PSSA [8].

Code motion on the flat list is much easier, since we are no longer required to reconstruct the graph to perform code motion, Instead of reconstructing the control flow graph for code motion, PSSA [8] allows instructions to be moved together directly.
